basis: Marrow disorder; thumb defects 3/3, renal agenesis 3/4 and hydrocephalus 3/4. GI atresias (~67%) and cardiac/endocrine anomalies omitted by cap; small samples.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive limb malformations are common (absent thumbs 3/3), but skeletal abnormalities are not required to define Fanconi anemia.

basis: Cardiac and skeletal abnormalities define Noonan syndrome; ptosis occurs in 77/136 (~57%), and bruising susceptibility supports hemostatic dysfunction in 32/56 (~57%).

decisions.haematologic: involved: hemostatic dysfunction is common; bruising susceptibility occurs in 32/56 (~57%). Overt abnormal bleeding at 3/18 measures a narrower manifestation.

basis: Defining dental malocclusion maps to gastrointestinal. Short stature alone establishes neither skeletal pathology nor an endocrine disorder.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage; no skeletal dysplasia or other structural locomotor abnormality is supplied.

basis: Emery-Dreifuss dystrophy is characterized by skeletal myopathy, contractures and cardiac conduction/myocardial disease. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish pulmonary damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac conduction disease or cardiomyopathy is a cardinal component of Emery-Dreifuss dystrophy; both are annotated here despite uncertain SYNE2-specific penetrance.

basis: Named brain and urinary tract malformations; reflux is frequent (30-79%). Metopic craniosynostosis is reported in 1/1, supporting skeletal involvement with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.renal: primary: urinary tract malformations are explicitly named and described as a characteristic component; vesicoureteral reflux occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: metopic synostosis is a structural skull abnormality reported in 1/1 annotated patient; the frequency estimate has substantial sampling uncertainty.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, hypogonadism/obesity and developmental impairment define the syndrome; stage 5 CKD occurs in 3/4. Polydactyly (2/2) omitted by cap; situs alone is noninjurious.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability and developmental delay are major diagnostic features of Bardet-Biedl syndrome and are present in 2/2 annotated patients.

basis: Vertebral/rib dysplasia with T-cell deficiency (1/1); thoracic respiratory dysfunction 2/2 and cardiac defects 1/1. Cleft palate and tethered cord omitted by cap; tiny samples.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: absent circulating T cells with recurrent bacterial and severe CMV infections (1/1) establishes immunodeficiency, requiring the mechanism axis.

basis: Skin peeling, nail abnormalities, keratoses and cheilitis define PLACK. Cheilitis occurs in 2-3/4 and oral leukoplakia in 2/4.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cheilitis is explicitly part of the syndrome's defining name; associated oral leukoplakia occurs in 2/4 patients.

basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize partial trisomy 10p; skeletal and visceral malformations vary with the duplicated segment, without established group-wide frequency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal malformations vary with duplication extent; the supplied evidence does not establish a defining skeletal disorder or involvement in at least ~30% across this umbrella.

basis: Malignant T-cell precursors occupy blood and marrow; leukemic liver infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly half. A thymic mediastinal mass does not establish pulmonary involvement.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration causing hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 40-60%; direct malignant occupation qualifies without requiring hepatic failure.
